candidate.hyperbolic_necessity: The observed directedness is consistent with branching, non-reciprocal transitions: a negatively curved hierarchy can provide increasing representational capacity for separated branches as codes refine, rather than forcing all branches into a uniformly scaled Euclidean neighborhood. This is a geometric hypothesis for reducing prefix collisions, not a causal conclusion from the manifest and not a claim that asymmetry mathematically proves negative curvature is necessary.

math_definition.architecture: For each item i, content embedding e_i is passed through the existing content encoder to h_i in R^32. Quantize h_i into exactly three residual levels, each with 256 learned code vectors a[l,k] in R^32. The one global item SID is (k[i,1],k[i,2],k[i,3]); it is not user- or event-specific.
math_definition.conditioning: No level conditions on earlier discrete codes. Residual levels condition only on the continuous residual formed by subtracting the previously assigned code vectors in level order.
math_definition.fixed_geometry: Set c=1.0, tau=1.0, epsilon=1e-5. For c>0 define exp_c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||)/(sqrt(c)*||v||) v, with multiplier 1 when ||v||=0. Define P_c(x)=x*min(1,(1-epsilon)/(sqrt(c)*||x||)), with scale 1 at ||x||=0. Define u_c(x,y)=2c||x-y||^2/((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2)); d_c^2(x,y)=[log1p(u_c+sqrt(u_c*(u_c+2)))]^2/c, the numerically stable arcosh(1+u) squared distance. Inputs to d must lie in the open ball; all mapped points are projected first. At c=0 define exp_0(v)=v, omit P_0 entirely because its radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined, and define d_0^2(x,y)=4||x-y||^2. These are the explicit c->0 limits of the same parameterized code path; there is no separate flat implementation.
math_definition.residual_assignment_order: For each item i and level l=1,2,3, initialize r[i,1]=h_i. At each level, in this exact order: map q=P_c(exp_c(r[i,l])); map every level-l code b[l,k]=P_c(exp_c(a[l,k])); assign k[i,l]=argmin over k in {1,...,256} of d_c^2(q,b[l,k]), breaking ties by smallest k; subtract in the original tangent coordinates r[i,l+1]=r[i,l]-a[l,k[i,l]]. No projection is applied after subtraction; the next level maps and projects its new residual. The level-l assigned reconstruction contribution is a[l,k[i,l]], and the complete tangent reconstruction is sum over l of those three contributions.
math_definition.training_loss: Let I be the train-split item index set and n=|I|. Let h_i in R^32 be encoder outputs, and let Q_i=sum_{l=1}^3 a[l,k[i,l]]. Define L=(1/n) sum_{i in I} [||sg(h_i)-Q_i||_2^2 + ||h_i-sg(Q_i)||_2^2], where sg is stop-gradient and the two terms are respectively codebook and commitment losses with coefficient 1.0 each; the first updates code vectors only and the second encoder only. Reduction is the item mean, with all train items included, so the group is nonempty; if I is empty the training step is skipped and loss is zero. There is no parameter-dependent target distribution: assignments are hard argmin indices computed from the current forward pass and treated as nondifferentiable constants, so no target/parameter circularity arises. Validation/test events and transitions are never used in this loss.

candidate.next_item_hypothesis: Train-only transitions exhibit strongly directed item flow: 314605 of 339519 directed transition observations have no observed reverse event (fraction 0.9266197178950221). A demonstrated failure to target is therefore Euclidean residual quantization collapsing distinct outgoing next-item branches into shared early prefixes, leaving downstream next-item ranking with less separable item identifiers. This statistic motivates but does not establish the failure; validation Hard-L1 error and prefix/collision diagnostics test whether it occurs. Stage2 builds item SIDs only; downstream T5 Stage3 ranks next items.
candidate.real_trigger_measurement: On the fixed validation item set, measure Hard-L1 reconstruction error over the three-level global SID, number of distinct two-token prefixes, L3 collision rate, refinement gain from adding L3, and conditional G3 as defined by the existing Stage2 evaluator. Report each against the matched c=0 arm. Test next-item ranking only in the frozen Stage3 evaluation; never use validation/test outcomes to train or choose Stage2 assignments.
candidate.training_only_inputs: Content embeddings and train-split item transitions only. Train-split transitions may be used as legal supervision under CLAUDE.md rule 16, but this candidate does not add a transition loss. No validation/test behavior, future events, prediction-time user context, or batch-composition signal is used.

behavior_problem_candidates.basis: TIGER (FULL_TEXT) provides an explicit behavioral target and semantic-ID decoder; HMamba and the listed hyperbolic sequential/session papers (ABSTRACT) provide evidence that hyperbolic representations are used for sequential preference or interaction behavior. HypRQ-VAE (ABSTRACT) suggests a current bridge between hyperbolic item indexing and generative recommendation.
behavior_problem_candidates.behavioral_evaluation: Evaluate next-item Recall/NDCG or MRR, separately reporting head/tail and cold-start items; compare against both a generative-SID baseline and hyperbolic sequential baseline. Avoid claiming behavior improvement from geometric fit alone.
behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Behavior-first next-item modeling with hyperbolic state/sequence representations and generative semantic-ID decoding
behavior_problem_candidates.overlap_status: No independently verified source inspected here demonstrates all three elements together: user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry, and generative semantic IDs.
behavior_problem_candidates.testable_question: Does replacing Euclidean item semantic-ID quantization and/or the sequence state space with a hyperbolic hierarchy improve next-item ranking and tail-item generalization, compared with TIGER-style Euclidean RQ-VAE semantic IDs and hyperbolic sequential baselines?

limitations: No verified full-text paper in this search directly establishes the complete three-way intersection. The strongest evidence is complementary: TIGER directly verifies next-item behavior plus generative semantic IDs, while the hyperbolic sequential papers verify the geometry/behavior side only at abstract level.

FULL_TEXT means an arXiv HTML full-text page was opened and relevant sections inspected; ABSTRACT means only arXiv abstract/search-result text was inspected. A listed PDF/full-text URL is a locator, not evidence that its content was read.

HypRQ-VAE appears highly relevant but abstract-level evidence alone does not establish next-item conditioning or a precise equivalence between its item index and TIGER-style semantic IDs. Verify its full text before asserting the full overlap.
The source set is a targeted intersection search, not a systematic review; absence of a full three-way match here is not proof that none exists.
No prior-candidate prompts, unseen future interactions, or test interactions were used.

manifest.research_question: Research verified literature where user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry and generative semantic IDs intersect.

sources.exact_overlap: Directly covers user next-item behavior and generative semantic IDs: a Transformer sequence-to-sequence model predicts the Semantic ID for the next item from a user's chronologically ordered interaction history. Full text describes content embeddings quantized into residual-quantized codeword tuples (RQ-VAE) and the next-item training objective (Sections 3.1–3.2). It does not use or report hyperbolic geometry; semantic hierarchy is learned with RQ-VAE, not a demonstrated hyperbolic manifold.
